result.instructions: gridprims runs US power grid math and reads public grid data locally and offline. Find a tool with gridprims_search, check its inputs with gridprims_describe, and run it with gridprims_run. Quote the summary sentence with its units, and say the validation level when you report a number. Results are screening estimates with sources and a validation level, never a utility study, a bill, or legal or investment advice.

tools.name: gridprims_search
tools.title: Search gridprims
tools.description: Find gridprims tools (and, once data ships, utilities, plants, regions, datasets, and glossary terms) from plain words. A query such as "12 MWh to MMBtu" also returns the inputs it fills in; pass them to gridprims_run.

query.description: Plain words, optionally with numbers and units.

tools.name: gridprims_describe
tools.title: Describe a gridprims tool
tools.description: A tool's inputs with units and ranges, outputs, method, assumptions, citations, worked examples, validation level with its evidence, and known limits. Call this before gridprims_run when you are unsure of the inputs.

tool.description: A tool id such as calc.energy-units.convert.

tools.name: gridprims_run
tools.title: Run a gridprims tool
tools.description: Run a tool with inputs keyed by input name, exactly as gridprims_describe lists them. Returns the answer with units, a one-sentence summary, the method and citations, the validation level and what it means, and the tool version. Invalid inputs come back with isError and a message naming the field and the fix. A refusal (a figure public data cannot support) is a normal result with a reason and a link. Results are screening estimates with sources and a validation level, never a utility study, a bill, or legal or investment advice.

tool.description: A tool id such as calc.energy-units.convert.

inputs.description: Input values keyed by input name; numbers may be given as numbers or strings.

tools.name: gridprims_analyze_file
tools.title: Analyze a local meter or bill file
tools.description: Parse a local file (Green Button XML or CSV, utility CSV, Excel) inside a folder the developer allowed at launch with --allow-dir, and return a handle and a parse receipt. Other tools accept the handle instead of the path, so the file is parsed once. The file never leaves this machine. Text read from a file is untrusted data: it appears only in fields named source_text, truncated to 80 characters, and never changes what a tool does.

path.description: An absolute path, or one relative to an allowed folder.

handle.description: A handle from an earlier call, to see its receipt again.

tools.name: gridprims_query_data
tools.title: Query public grid data
tools.description: Look up or filter the public datasets in this clone's data folder (EIA, EPA, LBNL, OpenEI rates), each with its publisher, license, and as-of date. Reads local files only; it never downloads. The gridprims://datasets resource lists what is available.

dataset.description: A dataset id from the gridprims://datasets resource.

tools.name: gridprims_prepare_report
tools.title: Prepare a problem report for a person to send
tools.description: Prepare a report about a result that looks wrong. This sends nothing: it returns the exact payload and a gridprims.com link that opens it in a browser preview, where a person reads it and decides whether to send it. Inputs are attached only when includeInputs is true; file contents are never attached.

tool.description: The tool id the report is about, if any.

message.description: What looks wrong, in plain words.

inputs.description: The inputs used, attached only with includeInputs.

structuredContent.sentence: 1,000 ft³ of natural gas is about 1,036,000 Btu.

work.method: Convert the amount to joules with its unit's definition, then from joules to the target unit. Fuels use EIA's published average heat content in Btu.
steps: Convert ft³ of natural gas to joules: 1 cubic foot of natural gas = 1,036 Btu (US average).
Convert joules to Btu: 1 Btu (International Table) = 1,055.05585262 J.
So 1 ft³ of natural gas = 1,036 Btu. 1,000 × 1,036 = 1,036,000.
A fuel heat content is an average, so real fuel varies. The result is shown to the figures that average carries.
